input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of Deliverables — bespoke work product created specifically for Customer, expressly excluding Vendor Technology and know-how under § 1.4 — in Vendor, leaving Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence that ends with the Order Form term. That contradicts the preferred position that Customer owns what it pays for and sits close to the walk-away zone. Sections 14.1 (Customer Data and Customer IP), 14.3 (Vendor retains Vendor Technology with the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence-back) and 14.4 (no joint ownership) are acceptable, so the fix is confined to 14.2: flip ownership to Customer with an express irrevocable assignment and redirect the limited term licence to Vendor, leaving all other wording intact.

proposal.summary: Flip Deliverable ownership to Customer via Vendor assignment; the limited term licence now runs to Vendor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the bespoke work product we pay for, so we have flipped Deliverable ownership to Customer with an express assignment from Vendor and pointed the limited term licence at Vendor instead. Vendor's platform IP is untouched — Section 14.3 keeps Vendor Technology with Vendor under the Section 13.2 perpetual licence; if Vendor cannot assign, our fallback is Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables.
